items.excerpt: Am I Audio has launched I Am Choir, an AI vocal plug-in that turns a single vocal take into a full choral arrangement. It was built with singers who were credited, compensated and share in royalties — a consent-first model for AI vocal tooling.

Suno has announced Suno Vinyl, a service that presses tracks from a user's AI-generated library onto custom 12-inch records with designed sleeves, around $45 per record. Prompt-made music gets a physical, art-directed output format.

Federico Pepe's Push Hack opens up Ableton Push 3's display, file system, MIDI and LEDs via SSH — and he built it with AI-assisted coding agents, arguing reverse-engineering is exactly what ML is good at. A concrete look at AI agents as instrument-modding tools.

Empire Of The Sun's Luke Steele says "of course" he uses AI in his process and warns artists who refuse it that it will "come and swallow you". A working-artist read on where AI sits inside a real creative workflow.
Quiet Riot / Ozzy Osbourne bassist Rudy Sarzo breaks down how he actually uses AI to make new music and why — a veteran player's practical account of folding generative tools into recording.

Spotify says it doesn't need every major label on board to ship its AI covers and remixes product, hours after signing Merlin. Signals the fan-remix creation tool is close to a real launch. [ALT of items 7 & 8 — same story]

Merlin, representing 30,000+ independent labels, joins Universal in backing Spotify's AI-powered remix and covers product. The paid tool will let fans generate AI covers and remixes of opted-in artists, with credit and compensation attached. [ALT of items 6 & 8]

Spotify and Merlin sign a licensing agreement covering the streamer's AI remixing tool for Premium subscribers, widening the indie catalogue that fans will be able to rework generatively. [ALT of items 6 & 7]

Google's Flow Music Spaces update folds song generation, editing, stem splitting and video creation into one AI workspace — the case that Google is assembling an all-in-one AI music studio rather than a single generator.

A Billboard-charting single by LA rapper Fenix Flexin is being called AI-generated by listeners pointing at "telltale" artefacts; the rapper denies it. A live test of whether audiences can hear the difference — and of what disclosure norms are worth.

A Kapwing study finds the biggest AI music acts have already built streaming audiences worth millions on Spotify and YouTube — and are still growing. Data on how far synthetic artists have already moved into the mainstream.

The IFPI sets out three principles governing when a recording made with generative AI can qualify for the charts — a concrete disclosure standard creators will have to declare against. [DUP-RISK: adjacent to the already-carded 'labels propose AI chart rules' story]

The EU AI Act's transparency rules came into force on 2 August, and Music Ally breaks down what they mean in practice — most immediately for the AI tools musicians already use, including labelling of AI-generated output. [DUP-RISK: overlaps AI-labelling coverage]
